 ATP Finals Tennis Best Bets & Predictions for Friday, November 20
 Today’s ATP Finals picks, with matchup analysis and betting insights for Friday, November 20. 
 By Zachary Cohen - November 19, 2026 6732 
 X Facebook Email 
 Looking for the best bets for the ATP Finals on Friday, November 20? We break down the day’s matches, analyzing form, playing styles, and the odds to find our favorite picks for the action in Turin, Italy. Here’s what we’re betting on — and why.
 MORE: Check out Gill Alexander’s ATP Finals best bets on our Pro Picks page! 
 Flavio Cobolli vs. Carlos Alcaraz
Frances Tiafoe vs. Daniil Medvedev
 I hate that I keep giving out square-looking moneyline parlays, but I’ll do whatever it takes to land on something I’m comfortable with. On a strange Friday in Turin, that means a two-favorite parlay for the final round-robin matches.
 Alcaraz is dealing with pain in his left hamstring and right knee. He felt the hamstring in the second set of his win over Medvedev, took a medical timeout, and had his thigh heavily strapped. He then skipped Thursday’s practice to get an MRI. The reporting out of Spain is extremely positive, with Marca and COPE saying he’s cleared to continue and will be monitored day by day. That’s why I gave out Alcaraz to win the ATP Finals at +108 on “A Numbers Game” during my weekly Thursday-morning spot.
 His matchup with Cobolli is a dead rubber. Alcaraz has already clinched the Lendl Group, and Cobolli is eliminated. Tournament rules still require Alcaraz to play, because skipping would mean disqualification. That adds a wrinkle: if he flares up, he could retire mid-match and still be fit for the semifinals. As long as he’s healthy, though, it’s hard to imagine him losing to Cobolli, especially on anything but clay. Check your shop’s retirement rules before you bet.
 I’m essentially using Alcaraz to get a better price on the Medvedev moneyline, since -225 is too rich for my blood. I’m also not looking to play the spread, because both Medvedev and Tiafoe are volatile. The match itself is an elimination match: the winner takes the semifinal spot against Zverev, whatever the score. That means both players will be motivated. But with the Alcaraz tie-in, we’re basically getting Medvedev at -132. Sign me up for that. 
 Medvedev leads the head-to-head 6-2. He’s also the better returner and more reliable baseliner. On top of that, he’s serving just as well as Tiafoe, if not better, in 2026. He’d need to play very poorly to lose this match. 
 PARLAY: Alcaraz ML & Medvedev ML (-132)

 I usually have A LOT MORE on the Pro Picks page . These plays count towards my record and have been a big part of my success this season. Make sure you check them out. I’ll probably add a few more over there, so refresh that page throughout the day if you’re looking for action. That’s also where I put my Challenger-level plays, as well as picks for lower level ATP and WTA events.
